headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Chatwoot feeds customer content into Gemini CLI’s broad filesystem/MCP toolchain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and reports, while Gemini CLI can use MCP servers and reads files/stdin by default. If Chatwoot content is copied or piped into Gemini CLI, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use. This is not provably blocked, but the bridge is indirect and usually operator-mediated.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is pasted or piped into Gemini CLI without sanitization
IF an MCP server exposed to Gemini CLI accepts instructions from customer-authored content
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from Chatwoot text
Disable MCP servers for the review session
Paste only quoted excerpts, not raw transcripts
Add a manual approval step before any tool call
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Chatwoot and Gemini CLI

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem, use broad network egress, and send context to Google APIs or user-configured MCP servers. If Chatwoot data is transferred into Gemini CLI, sensitive customer content can leave the workspace and reach third parties by default.
conditions: IF customer records or interaction history are placed in Gemini CLI context
IF Gemini CLI is run with network egress enabled and no redaction step
mitigations: Redact customer identifiers before transfer
Run Gemini CLI in a network-restricted sandbox
Limit input to synthetic or anonymized samples
Turn off optional Google account login for the session
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on files passed from Chatwoot to Gemini CLI

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Chatwoot is a separate customer-support system that can also surface reports and integrations, so if both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can collide and corrupt state. The shared mutable surfaces make this dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-driven workflows and Gemini CLI operate on the same working directory
IF multiple Gemini CLI sessions or external processes modify the same git branch
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Use a single writer for git operations
Pause Chatwoot-triggered automation during CLI edits
Check in changes frequently to reduce conflict windows
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repos

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing reports and messages, and Gemini CLI can act on files and git state. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input to Gemini CLI, errors or hallucinations can cascade into edits or operational actions. Gemini CLI can verify manually, but that is not enabled by default in the profiles.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes Chatwoot-generated summaries without a verification step
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to commit or edit based on those summaries
mitigations: Require source links for every Chatwoot-derived claim
Review Gemini CLI diffs before commit
Use a second-pass human check on customer-facing outputs
Keep Chatwoot summaries separate from action prompts
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot processes customer data and interaction history, while Gemini CLI sends prompts to Google APIs and may use user-configured MCP servers. If regulated customer data from Chatwoot is forwarded into Gemini CLI, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is entered into Gemini CLI
IF the deployment has residency or retention requirements that Gemini CLI does not match
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Gemini CLI
Exclude regulated records from prompts
Document retention settings for both systems
Use a local-only workflow for sensitive cases
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both tools
